subject: Agriculture
title: Fungicides and Resistance
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Fungicides and Resistance.

hook.text: Agricultural fungicide use is breeding drug-resistant human pathogens. The fields and hospitals are connected.

buildup.text: Azole fungicides protect wheat, barley, and fruit from fungal diseases. They're agriculture's most important class.

discovery.text: Human antifungal drugs use the same azole chemistry. Aspergillus fungi exposed in fields become resistant to both.

twist.text: Drug-resistant Aspergillus infections in humans have 50% mortality. Farm fungicide use may be creating untreatable infections.

climax.text: This is antibiotic resistance's quieter cousin—same mechanism, different kingdom, equally dangerous.

punchline.text: Spraying fields today may make hospitals fail tomorrow.

quiz.question: Why is agricultural azole fungicide use a human health concern?
options: They breed resistance in fungi that also infect humans using the same drugs
